title: ENDEX: 09:45 Wednesday, Intake Closed, Mile 31 Rebuild Under Way

fields.resolution: ENDEX. It is 09:45 CDT on Wednesday 9 June 2027. Boom from the Wichita depot is on the road to rebuild the mile 31 deflection station and should arrive about 12:30. The sections released from mile 9.5 are holding the re-sheen at the mile 33 deflection station. The Sterling Bluff intake stays closed and conservation stays in effect until three things are in: the 08:30 and 09:30 sample results, the Environmental Unit's recommendation and KDHE concurrence. KDWP is keeping the Mill Ridge boat ramp and the Kaw Valley Fishing Access closed. This ends the exercise.
finalState: Volume: 2,900–3,300 bbl of medium sour crude (SCADA volume balance VB-0621). This is an estimate, not a confirmed figure. The cause is still unknown.
TRJ-03 (model run 09:30 CDT) replaces TRJ-02 and covers the re-release from mile 31 and Cottonwood Slough at mile 22.
The wildlife status report has gone to USFWS and KDWP. The NRC update on report 1398274 and PHMSA's records request are both logged.
Sterling Bluff is on storage and wells with conservation in effect. Prairie Bend RWD is still buying water through the interconnect.
PREP record: this was the 3,100-bbl planning-range release. It was NOT a worst case discharge (the WCD for Prairie Bend is 8,400 bbl).
fields.hotWashTransition: Thank you, everyone. Please put down your phones, radios and ICS forms. Before we break, the Planning Section will complete the PREP exercise record. It lists the core components exercised (notifications, OSRO activation, sensitive-area protection, Unified Command, the JIC and wildlife) and the plan and scenario used. It records this as a 3,100-bbl planning-range release, not a worst case discharge. We will take ten minutes and then start the hot wash.
fields.hotWashMethod: Timeline walk-back, then 3-Up, 3-Down. First rebuild the notification log against the clock: who was called, who was actually reached, and when. Then each section names three things that went well and three that broke.
hotWashQuestions: A general-line call or voicemail to the rural district or Sterling Bluff at 07:14 or 07:16 is not a notification, because their decision-makers were not reached until 07:47 and 07:52. What counts as notified in our plan, and who verifies it?
The volume was reported as 2,700–3,500 bbl, then 3,100 bbl, then 100,000 gallons in the media, and finally 2,900–3,300 bbl. Where did our one number with its basis hold, and where did it slip?
TRJ-02 gave arrival windows. How did they drive the boom sites and the intake decisions, and how did we find out the forecast was out of date after the mile 31 failure?
The ramp closure, the intake closures, the ditch burn and the 'water is safe' line all came up. Which of these did Ironbark try to decide when they belonged to KDWP, the utilities, the FOSC or KDHE?
Where would boom angled to the current, set earlier, have changed the outcome at Mill Ridge, mile 7 and mile 31?
fields.facilitatorNote: Collect the notification log, the ICS 202, 232 and 213 drafts, the JIC messages and the evaluator sheets before the break. Confirm that Planning's PREP record lists the core components and marks the scenario as not a WCD. Do not let the room argue about cause; the cause stays unknown.
